clue.text: Deliver a homily, quietly gaining measure of influence

parts.note: P is piano, the musical marking for playing quietly
your reach is how far your influence extends

explanation.surface: A preacher's sermon quietly extends their sway over the congregation.
explanation.definitionFit: To preach is to deliver a sermon, and a homily is a sermon.

clue.text: One offers a limited space for journalists

definitions.text: One offers a limited space for journalists

parts.words: One offers a limited space for journalists
parts.note: the press need a reserved spot at a sports ground; the cryptic touch is that a box is literally a bounded space

explanation.surface: Something provides cramped room for reporters.
explanation.definitionFit: A press box is the enclosed area at a stadium set aside for reporters.

clue.text: French art rogue returned property

parts.note: 'thou art' in French is 'tu es', so art is ES
a cheat is a rogue

explanation.surface: A dishonest dealer in French art gave back some property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'art' is the old form of 'are', not painting; French 'es' is that verb form.
explanation.definitionFit: Escheat is property that reverts to the state or lord when there is no heir.

clue.text: Person sending something, as opposed to one acknowledging delivery?

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
the recipient signs to acknowledge delivery

explanation.surface: The sender of a parcel contrasted with the one who signs for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A consigner dispatches goods to someone, so is the person sending them.

clue.text: Wrong to repeat a G&S work?

indicators.note: something wrong is out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: It seems a mistake to stage the same Gilbert and Sullivan piece twice.
explanation.walkthrough: Gilbert and Sullivan wrote comic operas such as The Mikado; the question mark admits that an operetta is only one example of what they wrote.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilbert and Sullivan's comic light operas are the classic examples of operettas.

clue.text: Top banana?

parts.note: bananas grow in bunches, and 'top banana' is slang for the best one or the boss

explanation.definitionFit: The pick of the bunch is the very best of a group, the top choice.

clue.text: Area of responsibility, issue king must get on top of

indicators.note: in a down answer the king's letter sits above the issue

parts.note: R is short for rex, king
to emit is to issue

explanation.surface: A king must master the issue in his area of responsibility.
explanation.definitionFit: A remit is the scope of a person's authority or task.

clue.text: Cats given restrictions, kept outside a B&B

indicators.note: the restrictions are kept round the outside of the rest

parts.note: ties are restrictions or constraints
the two Bs of bed and breakfast

explanation.surface: Pets are restrained outside a guesthouse.
explanation.walkthrough: A B&B is a bed-and-breakfast guesthouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabbies are striped domestic cats.

clue.text: 'You cannot trust what Capone says' — friends

parts.note: Al Capone was the Chicago gangster
what you cannot trust is lies

explanation.surface: A warning that the gangster's word is worthless, followed by a nod to his pals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You cannot trust what Capone says' amounts to 'Al lies'.
explanation.definitionFit: Allies are people on your side, friends.

clue.text: Christian dream about church leaders

indicators.note: about means moved around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Christian dreams about the heads of the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Archimandrites are senior abbots or clerics in the Eastern Orthodox church.

clue.text: City money leading to wealth, not half? Odd

indicators.note: the city and money pieces come before the next piece

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London
a cent is a small coin

indicators.note: only the first half of the six-letter word for wealth is kept, the rest dropped

parts.note: riches means wealth

explanation.surface: A query about City finance and the path to riches, with a dismissive 'Odd' at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' drops HES from RICHES, leaving RIC. The City of London is Britain's financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: An eccentric person or habit is unconventional, which is to say odd.

clue.text: Woman married the third man to come along

parts.words: the third man to come along
parts.note: in Genesis, Abel was born after Adam and Cain, the third man to exist

explanation.surface: A wife's marriage story: she wed the third suitor who turned up.
explanation.definitionFit: Mabel is a female first name, and crosswords use 'woman' for any such name.

clue.text: European is smart, journalist admitted

indicators.note: the journalist is let into the word for smart

parts.note: swish means smart or stylish
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A well-dressed continental lets a reporter in.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swede, or anything from Sweden, is European; the word serves as noun or adjective.

clue.text: Give a summary of unpopular policy

parts.note: out means out of fashion, unpopular
a party line is its policy

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to sketch an unpopular government policy.
explanation.definitionFit: To outline something is to describe its main points briefly, a summary.

clue.text: Playwright of some import once

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dramatist who once mattered a little.
explanation.walkthrough: Joe Orton was an English playwright of the 1960s, author of Loot and Entertaining Mr Sloane.
explanation.definitionFit: Joe Orton wrote black comedies for the stage, so he is a playwright.

clue.text: Partner cut long hair — one lying down in the bedroom?

definitions.text: one lying down in the bedroom?

indicators.note: the partner word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a mate is a partner
a tress is a long lock of hair

explanation.surface: A partner trims long hair, then someone lies down in the bedroom.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke: a mattress does not lie down in the human sense, it just lies flat on the bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A mattress lies flat on the bed frame, hence the playful 'one lying down'.

clue.text: Pierce tin? It's tricky — I'll get something

definitions.note: the definition is a phrase, the voice of the person receiving, standing for the noun

indicators.note: something tricky is awkward, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Opening a can is hard work, but a reward is promised.
explanation.definitionFit: A recipient is one who receives, so can say they'll get something.

clue.text: Methane planet has — breathing ultimately 'restricted'!

parts.note: Mars is a planet

indicators.note: the letter is confined inside the word has
ultimately points to the final letter of the word breathing

explanation.surface: A planet's atmosphere contains methane, making breathing difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: Marsh gas is the common name for methane produced by rotting vegetation.

clue.text: Lady left with gold, protected by criminal agent

indicators.note: the letters for left and gold are shielded inside the criminal agent

parts.note: a fence handles stolen goods for thieves
OR is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A woman left holding gold is sheltered by a crook's middleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Florence is a female first name, and 'lady' stands for any such name in crosswords.

clue.text: The location in Paris for a mathematician

definitions.meaning: ... is French for the place or location

explanation.definitionFit: Laplace, the French scholar of celestial mechanics, bears a name that is French for 'the square'.

clue.text: Firm needing endless fuel to produce drink

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: the fuel word loses its final letter

parts.note: coal is a fuel

explanation.surface: A business runs short of fuel but still makes a hot drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocoa is a hot chocolate drink made from cacao powder.

clue.text: Dogs I have not seen as separate characters?

parts.note: curs are mongrel dogs
I've is short for I have

explanation.surface: Someone notes that dogs they own have never been seen alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Cursive handwriting joins its letters, so they are not seen as separate characters.

clue.text: Cat — it's wandering around rooms

indicators.note: wandering suggests going all over, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cat roams about the rooms of a house.
explanation.definitionFit: Attics are rooms in the roof space of a house.

clue.text: Time to get exceptional priest, one to offer advice

indicators.note: exceptional suggests out of the ordinary, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unusual priest has time to give counsel.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipster gives tips, especially on racing or shares, which is advice.

clue.text: Fish in river caught by one hoping to make profit?

indicators.note: the river letter is held inside the other word

parts.note: a ticket tout resells tickets at a mark-up

explanation.surface: A fish in a river is caught by someone fishing for gain.
explanation.walkthrough: A tout is a British term for a ticket scalper.
explanation.definitionFit: Trout are freshwater fish of the salmon family.

clue.text: Officials probing Trump I respect

indicators.note: the answer probes into the words, lying inside them

explanation.surface: Officials looking into Donald Trump, whom someone says they respect.
explanation.definitionFit: Umpires are the officials who judge play in sports such as cricket and tennis.

clue.text: This writer's past rendered in adult form

parts.note: the setter speaking: this writer is I, so 'this writer's' is I'M, I am
ago means in the past

explanation.surface: An author's past life is told in grown-up form.
explanation.definitionFit: An imago is the final mature stage of an insect after metamorphosis.

clue.text: Labelling to get sign of approval, say, on outside of container

parts.note: a tick marks something as correct

indicators.note: the letters for 'say' are placed around the container

parts.note: EG, for example, is what 'say' means
a tin is a container

explanation.surface: Putting labels on a container earns a tick of approval.
explanation.definitionFit: Ticketing is attaching tickets or tags to goods, which is labelling them.

clue.text: Most angelic son facing little ordeal

indicators.note: the son comes in front of what follows

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little
a test is a trial or ordeal

explanation.surface: A saintly boy faces a small trial.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweetest is the superlative of sweet, as in kind and gentle, so most angelic.

clue.text: Ship embodying very French emphasis

indicators.note: the ship holds the French word within it

parts.note: SS is steamship
tres is French for very

explanation.surface: A vessel carries a strong French accent.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress is the weight put on a word or idea, which is emphasis.
